props.covers: The descriptive grid pattern: RxC identical cells filled in row-major order, with one gap= value repeated exactly; cells keep row and column identity, anchoring later placement.

text.insert: In this descriptive notation, the main value is

— the one shared gap repeated exactly between cells. Children are item lines in row-major order; the count must fit the lattice (more than (R−1)×C, at most R×C). Cells keep their row and column identity, and that skeleton anchors everything placed later. On the live board, same size plus the same gap signals peers: choose the gap from content and corridor needs, then copy exact geometry across the group. The crowding diagnostic warns below about 80px between side-by-side sibling boxes or 96px between stacked siblings; those measurements are the physical floor for wires and labels, not prescribed spacing.
